text: Extra practice problems 1. The demand curve in the U.S. market for puppies is Q = 300 — P. The supply function for an appendectomy is Qs = 90 + 13P. (Quantity is measured in thousands.) a. What is the equilibrium price and quantity of an appendectomy? Answer: P=15, 0=285 b, Calculate consumer and producer surplus in this market. Answer: CS = $40.6 million. PS = $3.1 million. c. Suppose the government banned the sale of puppies. Puppies can be given away but not bought or sold. Calculate consumer surplus. Answer: This is equivalent 1o setting a price ceiling of 0. The first step is to find the new Pand Q. P is 0 by construction. Q is the quantity sellers are willing to produce at this price: Qs = 90 + 13(0) = 90 thousand puppies. There is a shortage of 300-90=210 thousand puppies. Consumer surplus is now $22.95 million. Producer surplus is $311K. d. What is the deadweight loss due to this government policy? Answer: The easiest way to find this is to subtract the new producer and consumer surplus from the old social surplus. Drawing a figure will show you why this is true. The answer is $20.4 million
